set.body:
VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, and it is pointedly ironic: the API review singled out R/crossnobis.R:230-232 as the BEST message in the package - the only one of 986 stop() calls containing runnable code - and proposed it as the template for rewriting the other 985. Following it does not work.

THE MESSAGE, raised when a user passes identity_metric() to plan_crossnobis():

  A learned crossnobis plan requires a residual-derived precision recipe;
  use `noise_precision(diag(...))` for a fixed identity metric.

FOLLOWING IT LITERALLY, both ways:

  plan_crossnobis(fit, fr, pr, metric = noise_precision(diag(P)))
    -> ERROR: argument "domain" is missing, with no default

  plan_crossnobis(fit, fr, pr, metric = noise_precision(diag(P), domain = domain))
    -> ERROR: Metric-recipe fields are missing or noncanonical.

So the advice fails twice over. The code as literally written in the message does not run, because noise_precision() has a required domain argument the message omits. And once the user supplies it, the resulting object is REJECTED BY THE VERY FUNCTION THAT RECOMMENDED IT.

THE CAUSE. There are two metric families and the message crosses them:

  effect_metric_recipe   identity_metric(), shrinkage_precision(), diagonal_precision()
                         -> what plan_crossnobis() accepts
  fixed neural metric    noise_precision(), neural_metric()
                         -> what plan_geometry() accepts

noise_precision() builds a FIXED metric. plan_crossnobis() requires a RECIPE. The message directs the user from the recipe family into the fixed family while they are calling the function that only takes recipes.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS, confirmed: shrinkage_precision(0.2) and diagonal_precision() both accepted.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN UNHELPFUL MESSAGE. The 143 invariant-family messages on bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM waste a user's time but do not misdirect. This one actively routes a user into a dead end, with the authority of being the most specific and most helpful-looking message in the package. A user who trusts it will conclude that crossnobis with a fixed identity metric is broken, when in fact they simply cannot get there from this constructor.

It also undermines the remediation plan on bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM, which proposed this message as the house template. The template needs fixing before it is copied 40 times.

FIX, one of:
  1. name a recipe that exists - identity_metric() is itself accepted elsewhere, and
     diagonal_precision() works - rather than noise_precision()
  2. if a fixed identity metric genuinely is unreachable through plan_crossnobis, say so and
     name plan_geometry(metric = neural_metric(...)) as the path that supports it
  3. at minimum, include the required domain argument in the suggested call

SEPARATELY, this is the third instance today of the fixed-versus-recipe seam causing trouble, after cross_partitions() on a fit (bd-01KZYDTPTS6QPHCM07P1PPH396) and plan_geometry refusing a fit. The metric families, the relation/fit boundary, and the geometry/crossnobis split are all the same seam viewed from different sides, and it is the least documented part of the package.
set.title: The one error message containing runnable code gives advice that cannot work
